413.para: though of course they were daughters of asses too. The same effect is attained by the use of diminutives, which make a bad thing less bad and a good thing less good. Take, for instance, the banter of Aristophanes in the Babylonians where he uses 'goldlet' for 'gold', 'cloaklet' for 'cloak', 'scoffiet' for 'scoff, and 'plaguelet'. But alike in using epithets and in using diminutives we must be wary and must observe the mean.

414.para: Bad taste in language may take any of four forms: (1) The misuse of compound words. Lycophron, for instance, talks of the 'many visaged heaven' above the 'giant-crested earth', and again the 'strait-pathed shore'; and Gorgias of the 'pauper-poet flatterer' and 'oath-breaking and over-oath-keeping'. Alcidamas uses such expressions as 'the soul filling with rage and face becoming flame-flushed', and 'he thought their enthusiasm would be issue-fraught' and 'issue-fraught he made the persuasion of his words', and 'sombre-hued is the floor of the sea'.The way all these words are compounded makes th

415.para: (2) Another is the employment of strange words. For instance, Lycophron talks of 'the prodigious Xerxes' and 'spoliative Sciron'; Alcidamas of 'a toy for poetry' and 'the witlessness of nature', and says 'whetted with the unmitigated temper of his spirit'.

416.para: (3) A third form is the use of long, unseasonable, or frequent epithets. It is appropriate enough for a poet to talk of 'white milk', in prose such epithets are sometimes lacking in appropriateness or, when spread too thickly, plainly reveal the author turning his prose into poetry. Of course we must use some epithets, since they lift our style above the usual level and give it an air of distinction. But we must aim at the due mean, or the result will be worse than if we took no trouble at all; we shall get something actually bad instead of something merely not good. That is why the epithets o

417.para: The ordinary use of compound words is where there is no term for a thing and some compound can be easily formed, like 'pastime' (chronotribein); but if this is much done, the prose character disappears entirely. We now see why the language of compounds is just the thing for writers of dithyrambs, who love sonorous noises; strange words for writers of epic poetry, which is a proud and stately affair; and metaphor for iambic verse, the metre which (as has been already' said) is widely used to-day.

418.para: (4) There remains the fourth region in which bad taste may be shown, metaphor. Metaphors like other things may be inappropriate. Some are so because they are ridiculous; they are indeed used by comic as well as tragic poets. Others are too grand and theatrical; and these, if they are far-fetched, may also be obscure. For instance, Gorgias talks of 'events that are green and full of sap', and says 'foul was the deed you sowed and evil the harvest you reaped'. That is too much like poetry. Alcidamas, again, called philosophy 'a fortress that threatens the power of law', and the Odyssey 'a goodly

419.para: The Simile also is a metaphor; the difference is but slight. When the poet says of Achilles that he

420.para: "Leapt on the foe as a lion, "

421.para: this is a simile; when he says of him 'the lion leapt', it is a metaphor-here, since both are courageous, he has transferred to Achilles the name of 'lion'. Similes are useful in prose as well as in verse; but not often, since they are of the nature of poetry. They are to be employed just as metaphors are employed, since they are really the same thing except for the difference mentioned.

422.para: The following are examples of similes. Androtion said of Idrieus that he was like a terrier let off the chain, that flies at you and bites you-Idrieus too was savage now that he was let out of his chains. Theodamas compared Archidamus to an Euxenus who could not do geometry-a proportional simile, implying that Euxenus is an Archidamus who can do geometry. In Plato's Republic those who strip the dead are compared to curs which bite the stones thrown at them but do not touch the thrower, and there is the simile about the Athenian people, who are compared to a ship's captain who is strong but a l

423.para: Such, then, are the ingredients of which speech is composed. The foundation of good style is correctness of language, which falls under five heads. (1) First, the proper use of connecting words, and the arrangement of them in the natural sequence which some of them require. For instance, the connective 'men' (e.g. ego men) requires the correlative de (e.g. o de). The answering word must be brought in before the first has been forgotten, and not be widely separated from it; nor, except in the few cases where this is appropriate, is another connective to be introduced before the one required. 425.para: Diviners use these vague generalities about the matter in hand because their predictions are thus, as a rule, less likely to be falsified. We are more likely to be right, in the game of 'odd and even', if we simply guess 'even' or 'odd' than if we guess at the actual number; and the oracle-monger is more likely to be right if he simply says that a thing will happen than if he says when it will happen, and therefore he refuses to add a definite date. All these ambiguities have the same sort of effect, and are to be avoided unless we have some such object as that mentioned. (4) A fourth rule is

This cannot be so where there are many connecting words or clauses, or where punctuation is hard, as in the writings of Heracleitus. To punctuate Heracleitus is no easy task, because we often cannot tell whether a particular word belongs to what precedes or what follows it. Thus, at the outset of his treatise he says, 'Though this truth is always men understand it not', where it is not clear with which of the two clauses the word 'always' should be joined by the punctuation. Further, the follo

427.para: The following suggestions will help to give your language impressiveness. (1) Describe a thing instead of naming it: do not say 'circle', but 'that surface which extends equally from the middle every way'. To achieve conciseness, do the opposite-put the name instead of the description. When mentioning anything ugly or unseemly, use its name if it is the description that is ugly, and describe it if it is the name that is ugly. (2) Represent things with the help of metaphors and epithets, being careful to avoid poetical effects. (3) Use plural for singular, as in poetry, where one finds

429.para: though only one haven is meant, and

431.para: (4) Do not bracket two words under one article, but put one article with each; e.g. 'that wife of ours.' The reverse to secure conciseness; e.g. 'our wife.' Use plenty of connecting words; conversely, to secure conciseness, dispense with connectives, while still preserving connexion; e.g. 'having gone and spoken', and 'having gone, I spoke', respectively. (6) And the practice of Antimachus, too, is useful-to describe a thing by mentioning attributes it does not possess; as he does in talking of Teumessus

433.para: A subject can be developed indefinitely along these lines. You may apply this method of treatment by negation either to good or to bad qualities, according to which your subject requires. It is from this source that the poets draw expressions such as the 'stringless' or 'lyreless' melody, thus forming epithets out of negations. This device is popular in proportional metaphors, as when the trumpet's note is called 'a lyreless melody'.

434.para: Your language will be appropriate if it expresses emotion and character, and if it corresponds to its subject. 'Correspondence to subject' means that we must neither speak casually about weighty matters, nor solemnly about trivial ones; nor must we add ornamental epithets to commonplace nouns, or the effect will be comic, as in the works of Cleophon, who can use phrases as absurd as 'O queenly fig-tree'. To express emotion, you will employ the language of anger in speaking of outrage; the language of disgust and discreet reluctance to utter a word when speaking of impiety or foulness; the lang

435.para: This aptness of language is one thing that makes people believe in the truth of your story: their minds draw the false conclusion that you are to be trusted from the fact that others behave as you do when things are as you describe them; and therefore they take your story to be true, whether it is so or not. Besides, an emotional speaker always makes his audience feel with him, even when there is nothing in his arguments; which is why many speakers try to overwhelm their audience by mere noise.

436.para: Furthermore, this way of proving your story by displaying these signs of its genuineness expresses your personal character. Each class of men, each type of disposition, will have its own appropriate way of letting the truth appear. Under 'class' I include differences of age, as boy, man, or old man; of sex, as man or woman; of nationality, as Spartan or Thessalian. By 'dispositions' I here mean those dispositions only which determine the character of a man's for it is not every disposition that does this. If, then, a speaker uses the very words which are in keeping with a particular dispositio

437.para: All the variations of oratorical style are capable of being used in season or out of season. The best way to counteract any exaggeration is the well-worn device by which the speaker puts in some criticism of himself; for then people feel it must be all right for him to talk thus, since he certainly knows what he is doing. Further, it is better not to have everything always just corresponding to everything else-your hearers will see through you less easily thus. I mean for instance, if your words are harsh, you should not extend this harshness to your voice and your countenance and have everyth

438.para: The form of a prose composition should be neither metrical nor destitute of rhythm. The metrical form destroys the hearer's trust by its artificial appearance, and at the same time it diverts his attention, making him watch for metrical recurrences, just as children catch up the herald's question, 'Whom does the freedman choose as his advocate?', with the answer 'Cleon!' On the other hand, unrhythmical language is too unlimited; we do not want the limitations of metre, but some limitation we must have, or the effect will be vague and unsatisfactory. Now it is number that limits all things; and

439.para: Of the various rhythms, the heroic has dignity, but lacks the tones of the spoken language. The iambic is the very language of ordinary people, so that in common talk iambic lines occur oftener than any others: but in a speech we need dignity and the power of taking the hearer out of his ordinary self. The trochee is too much akin to wild dancing: we can see this in tetrameter verse, which is one of the trochaic rhythms.

440.para: There remains the paean, which speakers began to use in the time of Thrasymachus, though they had then no name to give it. The paean is a third class of rhythm, closely akin to both the two already mentioned; it has in it the ratio of three to two, whereas the other two kinds have the ratio of one to one, and two to one respectively. Between the two last ratios comes the ratio of one-and-a-half to one, which is that of the paean.

441.para: Now the other two kinds of rhythm must be rejected in writing prose, partly for the reasons given, and partly because they are too metrical; and the paean must be adopted, since from this alone of the rhythms mentioned no definite metre arises, and therefore it is the least obtrusive of them. At present the same form of paean is employed at the beginning a at the end of sentences, whereas the end should differ from the beginning. There are two opposite kinds of paean, one of which is suitable to the beginning of a sentence, where it is indeed actually used; this is the kind that begins with a

444.para: The other paean begins, conversely, with three short syllables and ends with a long one, as

445.para: "meta de lan | udata t ok | eanon e | oanise nux. "

446.para: This kind of paean makes a real close: a short syllable can give no effect of finality, and therefore makes the rhythm appear truncated. A sentence should break off with the long syllable: the fact that it is over should be indicated not by the scribe, or by his period-mark in the margin, but by the rhythm itself.

447.para: We have now seen that our language must be rhythmical and not destitute of rhythm, and what rhythms, in what particular shape, make it so.

448.para: The language of prose must be either free-running, with its parts united by nothing except the connecting words, like the preludes in dithyrambs; or compact and antithetical, like the strophes of the old poets. The free-running style is the ancient one, e.g. 'Herein is set forth the inquiry of Herodotus the Thurian.' Every one used this method formerly; not many do so now. By 'free-running' style I mean the kind that has no natural stopping-places, and comes to a stop only because there is no more to say of that subject. This style is unsatisfying just because it goes on indefinitely-one alway

451.para: By a wrong division of the words the hearer may take the meaning to be the reverse of what it is: for instance, in the passage quoted, one might imagine that Calydon is in the Peloponnesus.

452.para: A Period may be either divided into several members or simple. The period of several members is a portion of speech (1) complete in itself, (2) divided into parts, and (3) easily delivered at a single breath-as a whole, that is; not by fresh breath being taken at the division. A member is one of the two parts of such a period. By a 'simple' period, I mean that which has only one member. The members, and the whole periods, should be neither curt nor long. A member which is too short often makes the listener stumble; he is still expecting the rhythm to go on to the limit his mind has fixed for i

It is either simply divided, as in 'I have often wondered at the conveners of national gatherings and the founders of athletic contests'; or it is antithetical, where, in each of the two members, one of one pair of opposites is put along with one of another pair, or the same word is used to bracket two opposites, as 'They aided both parties-not only those who stayed behind but those who accompanied them: for the latter they acquired new territory larger than that at home, and to the former they left territory at home that was la

475.para: We may now consider the above points settled, and pass on to say something about the way to devise lively and taking sayings. Their actual invention can only come through natural talent or long practice; but this treatise may indicate the way it is done. We may deal with them by enumerating the different kinds of them. We will begin by remarking that we all naturally find it agreeable to get hold of new ideas easily: words express ideas, and therefore those words are the most agreeable that enable us to get hold of new ideas. Now strange words simply puzzle us; ordinary words convey only what

We have still to explain what we mean by their 'seeing things', and what must be done to effect this. By 'making them see things' I mean using expressions that represent things as in a state of activity. Thus, to say that a good man is 'four-square' is certainly a metaphor; both the good man and the square are perfect; but the metaphor does not suggest activity. On the other hand, in the expression 'with his vigour in full bloom' there is a noti

481.para: where 'up sprang' gives us activity as well as metaphor, for it at once suggests swiftness. So with Homer's common practice of giving metaphorical life to lifeless things: all such passages are distinguished by the effect of activity they convey. Thus,

And the poet has attached these ideas to the things by means of proportional metaphors: as the stone is to Sisyphus, so is the shameless man to his victim. In his famous similes, too, he treats inanimate things in the same way:

492.para: Metaphors must be drawn, as has been said already, from things that are related to the original thing, and yet not obviously so related-just as in philosophy also an acute mind will perceive resemblances even in things far apart. Thus Archytas said that an arbitrator and an altar were the same, since the injured fly to both for refuge. Or you might say that an anchor and an overhead hook were the same, since both are in a way the same, only the one secures things from below and the other from above. And to speak of states as 'levelled' is to identify two widely different things, the equality o

493.para: Liveliness is specially conveyed by metaphor, and by the further power of surprising the hearer; because the hearer expected something different, his acquisition of the new idea impresses him all the more. His mind seems to say, 'Yes, to be sure; I never thought of that'. The liveliness of epigrammatic remarks is due to the meaning not being just what the words say: as in the saying of Stesichorus that 'the cicalas will chirp to themselves on the ground'. Well-constructed riddles are attractive for the same reason; a new idea is conveyed, and there is metaphorical expression. So with the 'nove

494.para: "Onward he came, and his feet were shod with his-chilblains, "

495.para: where one imagined the word would be 'sandals'. But the point should be clear the moment the words are uttered. Jokes made by altering the letters of a word consist in meaning, not just what you say, but something that gives a twist to the word used; e.g. the remark of Theodorus about Nicon the harpist Thratt' ei su ('you Thracian slavey'), where he pretends to mean Thratteis su ('you harpplayer'), and surprises us when we find he means something else. So you enjoy the point when you see it, though the remark will fall flat unless you are aware that Nicon is Thracian. Or again: Boulei auton pe

496.para: "Thou must not be a stranger stranger than Thou should'st. "

497.para: Do not the words 'thou must not be', &c., amount to saying that the stranger must not always be strange? Here again is the use of one word in different senses. Of the same kind also is the much-praised verse of Anaxandrides:

498.para: "Death is most fit before you do

499.para: "Deeds that would make death fit for you. "

500.para: This amounts to saying 'it is a fit thing to die when you are not fit to die', or 'it is a fit thing to die when death is not fit for you', i.e. when death is not the fit return for what you are doing. The type of language employed-is the same in all these examples; but the more briefly and antithetically such sayings can be expressed, the more taking they are, for antithesis impresses the new idea more firmly and brevity more quickly. They should always have either some personal application or some merit of expression, if they are to be true without being commonplace-two requirements not alwa

501.para: Successful similes also, as has been said above, are in a sense metaphors, since they always involve two relations like the proportional metaphor. Thus: a shield, we say, is the 'drinking-bowl of Ares', and a bow is the 'chordless lyre'. This way of putting a metaphor is not 'simple', as it would be if we called the bow a lyre or the shield a drinking-bowl. There are 'simple' similes also: we may say that a flute-player is like a monkey, or that a short-sighted man's eyes are like a lamp-flame with water dropping on it, since both eyes and flame keep winking. A simile succeeds best when it is

502.para: "Those legs of his curl just like parsley leaves; "

503.para: "Just like Philammon struggling with his punchball. "

504.para: These are all similes; and that similes are metaphors has been stated often already.

505.para: Proverbs, again, are metaphors from one species to another. Suppose, for instance, a man to start some undertaking in hope of gain and then to lose by it later on, 'Here we have once more the man of Carpathus and his hare', says he. For both alike went through the said experience.

506.para: It has now been explained fairly completely how liveliness is secured and why it has the effect it has. Successful hyperboles are also metaphors, e.g. the one about the man with a black eye, 'you would have thought he was a basket of mulberries'; here the 'black eye' is compared to a mulberry because of its colour, the exaggeration lying in the quantity of mulberries suggested. The phrase 'like so-and-so' may introduce a hyperbole under the form of a simile. Thus

507.para: "Just like Philammon struggling with his punchball "

508.para: is equivalent to 'you would have thought he was Philammon struggling with his punchball'; and

509.para: "Those legs of his curl just like parsley leaves "

510.para: is equivalent to 'his legs are so curly that you would have thought they were not legs but parsley leaves'. Hyperboles are for young men to use; they show vehemence of character; and this is why angry people use them more than other people.

511.para: "Not though he gave me as much as the dust

513.para: "But her, the daughter of Atreus' son, I never will marry,

514.para: "Nay, not though she were fairer than Aphrodite the Golden,

516.para: (The Attic orators are particularly fond of this method of speech.) Consequently it does not suit an elderly speaker.

517.para: It should be observed that each kind of rhetoric has its own appropriate style. The style of written prose is not that of spoken oratory, nor are those of political and forensic speaking the same. Both written and spoken have to be known. To know the latter is to know how to speak good Greek. To know the former means that you are not obliged, as otherwise you are, to hold your tongue when you wish to communicate something to the general public.

518.para: The written style is the more finished: the spoken better admits of dramatic delivery-like the kind of oratory that reflects character and the kind that reflects emotion. Hence actors look out for plays written in the latter style, and poets for actors competent to act in such plays. Yet poets whose plays are meant to be read are read and circulated: Chaeremon, for instance, who is as finished as a professional speech-writer; and Licymnius among the dithyrambic poets. Compared with those of others, the speeches of professional writers sound thin in actual contests. Those of the orators, on the

519.para: "Nireus likewise from Syme (three well-fashioned ships did bring),

520.para: "Nireus, the son of Aglaia (and Charopus, bright-faced king),

521.para: "Nireus, the comeliest man (of all that to Ilium's strand). "

522.para: If many things are said about a man, his name must be mentioned many times; and therefore people think that, if his name is mentioned many times, many things have been said about him. So that Homer, by means of this illusion, has made a great deal of though he has mentioned him only in this one passage, and has preserved his memory, though he nowhere says a word about him afterwards.

523.para: Now the style of oratory addressed to public assemblies is really just like scene-painting. The bigger the throng, the more distant is the point of view: so that, in the one and the other, high finish in detail is superfluous and seems better away. The forensic style is more highly finished; still more so is the style of language addressed to a single judge, with whom there is very little room for rhetorical artifices, since he can take the whole thing in better, and judge of what is to the point and what is not; the struggle is less intense and so the judgement is undisturbed. This is why the

524.para: To analyse style still further, and add that it must be agreeable or magnificent, is useless; for why should it have these traits any more than 'restraint', 'liberality', or any other moral excellence? Obviously agreeableness will be produced by the qualities already mentioned, if our definition of excellence of style has been correct. For what other reason should style be 'clear', and 'not mean' but 'appropriate'? If it is prolix, it is not clear; nor yet if it is curt. Plainly the middle way suits best. Again, style will be made agreeable by the elements mentioned, namely by a good blending

525.para: This concludes our discussion of style, both in its general aspects and in its special applications to the various branches of rhetoric. We have now to deal with Arrangement.

526.para: A speech has two parts. You must state your case, and you must prove it. You cannot either state your case and omit to prove it, or prove it without having first stated it; since any proof must be a proof of something, and the only use of a preliminary statement is the proof that follows it. Of these two parts the first part is called the Statement of the case, the second part the Argument, just as we distinguish between Enunciation and Demonstration. The current division is absurd. For 'narration' surely is part of a forensic speech only: how in a political speech or a speech of display can t

527.para: The Introduction is the beginning of a speech, corresponding to the prologue in poetry and the prelude in flute-music; they are all beginnings, paving the way, as it were, for what is to follow. The musical prelude resembles the introduction to speeches of display; as flute players play first some brilliant passage they know well and then fit it on to the opening notes of the piece itself, so in speeches of display the writer should proceed in the same way; he should begin with what best takes his fancy, and then strike up his theme and lead into it; which is indeed what is always done. (Take

528.para: The usual subject for the introductions to speeches of display is some piece of praise or censure. Thus Gorgias writes in his Olympic Speech, 'You deserve widespread admiration, men of Greece', praising thus those who start,ed the festival gatherings.' Isocrates, on the other hand, censures them for awarding distinctions to fine athletes but giving no prize for intellectual ability. Or one may begin with a piece of advice, thus: 'We ought to honour good men and so I myself am praising Aristeides' or 'We ought to honour those who are unpopular but not bad men, men whose good qualities have neve

529.para: "But now when allotment of all has been made... "

530.para: Introductions to speeches of display, then, may be composed of some piece of praise or censure, of advice to do or not to do something, or of appeals to the audience; and you must choose between making these preliminary passages connected or disconnected with the speech itself.

531.para: Introductions to forensic speeches, it must be observed, have the same value as the prologues of dramas and the introductions to epic poems; the dithyrambic prelude resembling the introduction to a speech of display, as

532.para: "For thee, and thy gilts, and thy battle-spoils.... "

533.para: In prologues, and in epic poetry, a foretaste of the theme is given, intended to inform the hearers of it in advance instead of keeping their minds in suspense. Anything vague puzzles them: so give them a grasp of the beginning, and they can hold fast to it and follow the argument. So we find-

534.para: "Sing, O goddess of song, of the Wrath...

535.para: "Tell me, O Muse, of the hero...

536.para: "Lead me to tell a new tale, how there came great warfare to Europe

538.para: The tragic poets, too, let us know the pivot of their play; if not at the outset like Euripides, at least somewhere in the preface to a speech like Sophocles-

540.para: and so in Comedy. This, then, is the most essential function and distinctive property of the introduction, to show what the aim of the speech is; and therefore no introduction ought to be employed where the subject is not long or intricate.

541.para: The other kinds of introduction employed are remedial in purpose, and may be used in any type of speech. They are concerned with the speaker, the hearer, the subject, or the speaker's opponent. Those concerned with the speaker himself or with his opponent are directed to removing or exciting prejudice. But whereas the defendant will begin by dealing with this sort of thing, the prosecutor will take quite another line and deal with such matters in the closing part of his speech. The reason for this is not far to seek. The defendant, when he is going to bring himself on the stage, must clear awa

542.para: The appeal to the hearer aims at securing his goodwill, or at arousing his resentment, or sometimes at gaining his serious attention to the case, or even at distracting it-for gaining it is not always an advantage, and speakers will often for that reason try to make him laugh.

543.para: You may use any means you choose to make your hearer receptive; among others, giving him a good impression of your character, which always helps to secure his attention. He will be ready to attend to anything that touches himself and to anything that is important, surprising, or agreeable; and you should accordingly convey to him the impression that what you have to say is of this nature. If you wish to distract his attention, you should imply that the subject does not affect him, or is trivial or disagreeable. But observe, all this has nothing to do with the speech itself. It merely has to do

544.para: "I will tell you that whose like you have never yet "

545.para: heard for terror, or for wonder. This is what Prodicus called 'slipping in a bit of the fifty-drachma show-lecture for the audience whenever they began to nod'. It is plain that such introductions are addressed not to ideal hearers, but to hearers as we find them. The use of introductions to excite prejudice or to dispel misgivings is universal-

546.para: "My lord, I will not say that eagerly... "

548.para: Introductions are popular with those whose case is weak, or looks weak; it pays them to dwell on anything rather than the actual facts of it. That is why slaves, instead of answering the questions put to them, make indirect replies with long preambles. The means of exciting in your hearers goodwill and various other feelings of the same kind have already been described. The poet finely says May I find in Phaeacian hearts, at my coming, goodwill and compassion; and these are the two things we should aim at. In speeches of display we must make the hearer feel that the eulogy includes either hims

549.para: The introductions of political oratory will be made out of the same materials as those of the forensic kind, though the nature of political oratory makes them very rare. The subject is known already, and therefore the facts of the case need no introduction; but you may have to say something on account of yourself or to your opponents; or those present may be inclined to treat the matter either more or less seriously than you wish them to. You may accordingly have to excite or dispel some prejudice, or to make the matter under discussion seem more or less important than before: for either of wh

550.para: In dealing with prejudice, one class of argument is that whereby you can dispel objectionable suppositions about yourself. It makes no practical difference whether such a supposition has been put into words or not, so that this distinction may be ignored. Another way is to meet any of the issues directly: to deny the alleged fact; or to say that you have done no harm, or none to him, or not as much as he says; or that you have done him no injustice, or not much; or that you have done nothing disgraceful, or nothing disgraceful enough to matter: these are the sort of questions on which the disp

551.para: "My tongue hath sworn: no oath is on my soul. "

552.para: Euripides said that his opponent himself was guilty in bringing into the law-courts cases whose decision belonged to the Dionysiac contests. 'If I have not already answered for my words there, I am ready to do so if you choose to prosecute me there.' Another method is to denounce calumny, showing what an enormity it is, and in particular that it raises false issues, and that it means a lack of confidence in the merits of his case. The argument from evidential circumstances is available for both parties: thus in the Teucer Odysseus says that Teucer is closely bound to Priam, since his mother He

553.para: There is another method open to both calumniator and apologist. Since a given action can be done from many motives, the former must try to disparage it by selecting the worse motive of two, the latter to put the better construction on it. Thus one might argue that Diomedes chose Odysseus as his companion because he supposed Odysseus to be the best man for the purpose; and you might reply to this that it was, on the contrary, because he was the only hero so worthless that Diomedes need not fear his rivalry.

554.para: We may now pass from the subject of calumny to that of Narration.

555.para: Narration in ceremonial oratory is not continuous but intermittent. There must, of course, be some survey of the actions that form the subject-matter of the speech. The speech is a composition containing two parts. One of these is not provided by the orator's art, viz. the actions themselves, of which the orator is in no sense author. The other part is provided by his namely, the proof (where proof is needed) that the actions were done, the description of their quality or of their extent, or even all these three things together. Now the reason why sometimes it is not desirable to make the whol

556.para: Nowadays it is said, absurdly enough, that the narration should be rapid. Remember what the man said to the baker who asked whether he was to make the cake hard or soft: 'What, can't you make it right?' Just so here. We are not to make long narrations, just as we are not to make long introductions or long arguments. Here, again, rightness does not consist either in rapidity or in conciseness, but in the happy mean; that is, in saying just so much as will make the facts plain, or will lead the hearer to believe that the thing has happened, or that the man has caused injury or wrong to some one,

557.para: You may also narrate as you go anything that does credit to yourself, e.g. 'I kept telling him to do his duty and not abandon his children'; or discredit to your adversary, e.g. 'But he answered me that, wherever he might find himself, there he would find other children', the answer Herodotus' records of the Egyptian mutineers. Slip in anything else that the judges will enjoy.

558.para: The defendant will make less of the narration. He has to maintain that the thing has not happened, or did no harm, or was not unjust, or not so bad as is alleged. He must therefor snot waste time about what is admitted fact, unless this bears on his own contention; e.g. that the thing was done, but was not wrong. Further, we must speak of events as past and gone, except where they excite pity or indignation by being represented as present. The Story told to Alcinous is an example of a brief chronicle, when it is repeated to Penelope in sixty lines. Another instance is the Epic Cycle as treated

559.para: The narration should depict character; to which end you must know what makes it do so. One such thing is the indication of moral purpose; the quality of purpose indicated determines the quality of character depicted and is itself determined by the end pursued. Thus it is that mathematical discourses depict no character; they have nothing to do with moral purpose, for they represent nobody as pursuing any end. On the other hand, the Socratic dialogues do depict character, being concerned with moral questions. This end will also be gained by describing the manifestations of various types of char

560.para: "But since my father and mother in their graves

561.para: "Lie dead, no brother can be born to me. "

562.para: If you have no such cause to suggest, just say that you are aware that no one will believe your words, but the fact remains that such is our nature, however hard the world may find it to believe that a man deliberately does anything except what pays him.

563.para: Again, you must make use of the emotions. Relate the familiar manifestations of them, and those that distinguish yourself and your opponent; for instance, 'he went away scowling at me'. So Aeschines described Cratylus as 'hissing with fury and shaking his fists'. These details carry conviction: the audience take the truth of what they know as so much evidence for the truth of what they do not. Plenty of such details may be found in Homer:

564.para: "Thus did she say: but the old woman buried her face in her hands: "

565.para: a true touch-people beginning to cry do put their hands over their eyes.

566.para: Bring yourself on the stage from the first in the right character, that people may regard you in that light; and the same with your adversary; but do not let them see what you are about. How easily such impressions may be conveyed we can see from the way in which we get some inkling of things we know nothing of by the mere look of the messenger bringing news of them. Have some narrative in many different parts of your speech; and sometimes let there be none at the beginning of it.

567.para: In political oratory there is very little opening for narration; nobody can 'narrate' what has not yet happened. If there is narration at all, it will be of past events, the recollection of which is to help the hearers to make better plans for the future. Or it may be employed to attack some one's character, or to eulogize him-only then you will not be doing what the political speaker, as such, has to do.

568.para: If any statement you make is hard to believe, you must guarantee its truth, and at once offer an explanation, and then furnish it with such particulars as will be expected. Thus Carcinus' Jocasta, in his Oedipus, keeps guaranteeing the truth of her answers to the inquiries of the man who is seeking her son; and so with Haemon in Sophocles.

569.para: The duty of the Arguments is to attempt demonstrative proofs. These proofs must bear directly upon the question in dispute, which must fall under one of four heads. (1) If you maintain that the act was not committed, your main task in court is to prove this. (2) If you maintain that the act did no harm, prove this. If you maintain that (3) the act was less than is alleged, or (4) justified, prove these facts, just as you would prove the act not to have been committed if you were maintaining that.

570.para: It should be noted that only where the question in dispute falls under the first of these heads can it be true that one of the two parties is necessarily a rogue. Here ignorance cannot be pleaded, as it might if the dispute were whether the act was justified or not. This argument must therefore be used in this case only, not in the others.

571.para: In ceremonial speeches you will develop your case mainly by arguing that what has been done is, e.g., noble and useful. The facts themselves are to be taken on trust; proof of them is only submitted on those rare occasions when they are not easily credible or when they have been set down to some one else.

572.para: In political speeches you may maintain that a proposal is impracticable; or that, though practicable, it is unjust, or will do no good, or is not so important as its proposer thinks. Note any falsehoods about irrelevant matters-they will look like proof that his other statements also are false. Argument by 'example' is highly suitable for political oratory, argument by 'enthymeme' better suits forensic. Political oratory deals with future events, of which it can do no more than quote past events as examples. Forensic oratory deals with what is or is not now true, which can better be demonstrat

573.para: Friend, you have spoken as much as a sensible man would have spoken. ,as much' says Homer, not 'as well'. Nor should you try to make enthymemes on every point; if you do, you will be acting just like some students of philosophy, whose conclusions are more familiar and believable than the premisses from which they draw them. And avoid the enthymeme form when you are trying to rouse feeling; for it will either kill the feeling or will itself fall flat: all simultaneous motions tend to cancel each other either completely or partially. Nor should you go after the enthymeme form in a passage where

574.para: Political oratory is a more difficult task than forensic; and naturally so, since it deals with the future, whereas the pleader deals with the past, which, as Epimenides of Crete said, even the diviners already know. (Epimenides did not practise divination about the future; only about the obscurities of the past.) Besides, in forensic oratory you have a basis in the law; and once you have a starting-point, you can prove anything with comparative ease. Then again, political oratory affords few chances for those leisurely digressions in which you may attack your adversary, talk about yourself, o

575.para: Now if you have proofs to bring forward, bring them forward, and your moral discourse as well; if you have no enthymemes, then fall back upon moral discourse: after all, it is more fitting for a good man to display himself as an honest fellow than as a subtle reasoner. Refutative enthymemes are more popular than demonstrative ones: their logical cogency is more striking: the facts about two opposites always stand out clearly when the two are nut side by side.

576.para: The 'Reply to the Opponent' is not a separate division of the speech; it is part of the Arguments to break down the opponent's case, whether by objection or by counter-syllogism. Both in political speaking and when pleading in court, if you are the first speaker you should put your own arguments forward first, and then meet the arguments on the other side by refuting them and pulling them to pieces beforehand. If, however, the case for the other side contains a great variety of arguments, begin with these, like Callistratus in the Messenian assembly, when he demolished the arguments likely to

577.para: "First, champion will I be of Goddesses...

579.para: where the speaker has attacked the silliest argument first. So much for the Arguments.

580.para: With regard to the element of moral character: there are assertions which, if made about yourself, may excite dislike, appear tedious, or expose you to the risk of contradiction; and other things which you cannot say about your opponent without seeming abusive or ill-bred. Put such remarks, therefore, into the mouth of some third person. This is what Isocrates does in the Philippus and in the Antidosis, and Archilochus in his satires. The latter represents the father himself as attacking his daughter in the lampoon

582.para: "Nor swear that it shall not befall... "

583.para: and puts into the mouth of Charon the carpenter the lampoon which begins

585.para: So too Sophocles makes Haemon appeal to his father on behalf of Antigone as if it were others who were speaking.

586.para: Again, sometimes you should restate your enthymemes in the form of maxims; e.g. 'Wise men will come to terms in the hour of success; for they will gain most if they do'. Expressed as an enthymeme, this would run, 'If we ought to come to terms when doing so will enable us to gain the greatest advantage, then we ought to come to terms in the hour of success.'

587.para: Next as to Interrogation. The best moment to a employ this is when your opponent has so answered one question that the putting of just one more lands him in absurdity. Thus Pericles questioned Lampon about the way of celebrating the rites of the Saviour Goddess. Lampon declared that no uninitiated person could be told of them. Pericles then asked, 'Do you know them yourself?' 'Yes', answered Lampon. 'Why,' said Pericles, 'how can that be, when you are uninitiated?'

588.para: Another good moment is when one premiss of an argument is obviously true, and you can see that your opponent must say 'yes' if you ask him whether the other is true. Having first got this answer about the other, do not go on to ask him about the obviously true one, but just state the conclusion yourself. Thus, when Meletus denied that Socrates believed in the existence of gods but admitted that he talked about a supernatural power, Socrates proceeded to to ask whether 'supernatural beings were not either children of the gods or in some way divine?' 'Yes', said Meletus. 'Then', replied Socrates

589.para: In replying, you must meet ambiguous questions by drawing reasonable distinctions, not by a curt answer. In meeting questions that seem to involve you in a contradiction, offer the explanation at the outset of your answer, before your opponent asks the next question or draws his conclusion. For it is not difficult to see the drift of his argument in advance. This point, however, as well as the various means of refutation, may be regarded as known to us from the Topics.

590.para: When your opponent in drawing his conclusion puts it in the form of a question, you must justify your answer. Thus when Sophocles was asked by Peisander whether he had, like the other members of the Board of Safety, voted for setting up the Four Hundred, he said 'Yes.'-'Why, did you not think it wicked?'-'Yes.'-'So you committed this wickedness?' 'Yes', said Sophocles, 'for there was nothing better to do.' Again, the Lacedaemonian, when he was being examined on his conduct as ephor, was asked whether he thought that the other ephors had been justly put to death. 'Yes', he said. 'Well then', as

591.para: As to jests. These are supposed to be of some service in controversy. Gorgias said that you should kill your opponents' earnestness with jesting and their jesting with earnestness; in which he was right. jests have been classified in the Poetics. Some are becoming to a gentleman, others are not; see that you choose such as become you. Irony better befits a gentleman than buffoonery; the ironical man jokes to amuse himself, the buffoon to amuse other people.

592.para: The Epilogue has four parts. You must (1) make the audience well-disposed towards yourself and ill-disposed towards your opponent (2) magnify or minimize the leading facts, (3) excite the required state of emotion in your hearers, and (4) refresh their memories.

593.para: (1) Having shown your own truthfulness and the untruthfulness of your opponent, the natural thing is to commend yourself, censure him, and hammer in your points. You must aim at one of two objects-you must make yourself out a good man and him a bad one either in yourselves or in relation to your hearers. How this is to be managed-by what lines of argument you are to represent people as good or bad-this has been already explained.

594.para: (2) The facts having been proved, the natural thing to do next is to magnify or minimize their importance. The facts must be admitted before you can discuss how important they are; just as the body cannot grow except from something already present. The proper lines of argument to be used for this purpose of amplification and depreciation have already been set forth.

595.para: (3) Next, when the facts and their importance are clearly understood, you must excite your hearers' emotions. These emotions are pity, indignation, anger, hatred, envy, emulation, pugnacity. The lines of argument to be used for these purposes also have been previously mentioned.

596.para: (4) Finally you have to review what you have already said. Here you may properly do what some wrongly recommend doing in the introduction-repeat your points frequently so as to make them easily understood. What you should do in your introduction is to state your subject, in order that the point to be judged may be quite plain; in the epilogue you should summarize the arguments by which your case has been proved. The first step in this reviewing process is to observe that you have done what you undertook to do. You must, then, state what you have said and why you have said it. Your method may b

597.para: For the conclusion, the disconnected style of language is appropriate, and will mark the difference between the oration and the peroration. 'I have done. You have heard me. The facts are before you. I ask for your judgement.'

615.para: 1. **抖音目标方向（FDE/公开做产品）没有 5 万粉以上的样本**：唯一 5 万+ 是同方向的教程号。 2. **量化指标全缺**：播放量、完播率、3 秒留存、私信转化都拿不到（未登录），四项判据全部"待校准"。 3. **转化入口拿不到**：橱窗、置顶、直播、私信自动回复在未登录下不渲染。 4. **跨平台未落库**：B站已搜到 12 个候选（含技术爬爬虾 B 站同名号），尚未建条目。 5. **YouTube / X / 小红书 / 视频号** 完全空白。

616.para: 面向「FDE 人设抖音账号」的竞品/对标资料库。纯 Markdown + 附件目录，不依赖任何私有格式，任何编辑器都能读，git 可直接管。

618.para: - 把散落在各个平台（抖音 / B站 / 小红书 / 视频号 / YouTube / X）的对标账号，统一成同一套字段，能横向比。 - 把"看到的"和"猜的"分开存：页面上直接可见的写【可见】，需要从入口反推的写【推断】，不混写。 - 分析结论不散落在聊天里，落到三个分区：内容方法论、变现路径、选题库。 - 每次新增素材只追加，不覆盖历史结论。

621.para: 1. 复制 [_templates/account.md](_templates/account.md) 到 `accounts/<平台>/<英文短名>.md`。 2. 文件名用平台内唯一、可读的英文/拼音短名（例：`laozhou-bababa.md`），避免中文和空格，保证链接不出错。 3. 按模板填字段。拿不准的字段写"未采集"，不要留空、不要猜。 4. 截图和抓取原文放进 `attachments/<平台>/<账号短名>/`，在条目里用相对路径引用。 5. 回到 [INDEX.md](INDEX.md) 加一行，并更新该平台的账号数与状态。

624.para: - 【可见】：在当前页面截图上能指出来。例：简介写了"合作加 V"、橱窗有 3 个商品、置顶视频挂了课程链接、直播间在卖课。 - 【推断】：页面没有明说，是从入口反推的。例：主页只有"商务合作"邮箱 + 系列视频结尾统一引导"评论区扣 1"，推断走的是私域承接。 - 推断必须写"依据是什么 + 置信度（高/中/低）"。没有依据的判断不进库。

663.section: ### 1. 欢喜的乡村小家(装修中)｜405 粉
663.para: ### 1. 欢喜的乡村小家(装修中)｜405 粉 - 单集 14 秒，纯口播 + 现场画面，一集只问一个决策（岩板还是石英石、780 一米）。 - 【可见】分集标题带"第 N 集"，但**没有统一栏目名**，靠合集串起来。 - 可迁移点：**一集一个决策 + 把选择权交给评论区**，这正是 FDE 第①段"让评论区出主意"的原生写法。 - 风险：14 秒装不下任何过程，只能装"选择题"。

664.para: ### 2. 赵三登｜1.3万 - 01:44，标题即钩子"我的翡翠创业日记！十年之约～"。 - 【可见】第 2 集"久违的拥抱"、第 3 集"没有经历过的人无法感同身受"——**用情绪节点当分集标题，不用进度当标题**。 - 可迁移点：把"第 N 集"从进度条改成情绪/转折点。

665.para: ### 4. 只想喝无糖冰红茶｜1.5万 - 00:29，系列名"30天卧推100kg"，第 1 集"全网人均卧推100kg教学"。 - 可迁移点：**时间盒 + 可验证数字**（30 天 / 100kg），观众知道什么时候能看到结果，天然追更。 - 对应 FDE：把"做一个 Agent"改写成"14 天把某流程自动化，目标是把 X 从 3 小时压到 10 分钟"。

666.para: ### 5. 这瓜子没肉｜512 粉 - 00:18，系列名"挑战捏100款"，每集一个成品。 - 可迁移点：**数量目标制造确定性更新**，第 N 集不需要剧情，只需要下一个编号。 - 风险：纯展示，没有冲突，完播靠好奇心，商业价值低。

667.para: ### 7. Dou.有米｜1.6万 - 05:57，第 1 集开头直接是崩溃事件（被顾客气到、重刷墙、100 块）。 - 可迁移点：**冲突第一句**——不介绍背景，先给"出事了"。 - 对应 FDE：客户现场翻车、上线当天崩了，这类真实事故是天然开头。

668.para: ### 8. 珍珍很忙｜1.1万 - 02:33，第 1 集标题是提问"大家觉得这次我们会成功吗？"。 - 可迁移点：**用未完成状态提问**，把观众拉进"陪跑"位置。

808.para: 刷屏一时的水果AI短剧，终究还是被整治了。

809.section: ## 抖快红B上最火的AI博主，在赚钱了吗？
809.para: “香蕉出轨草莓”、“蓝莓逆袭复仇”、“蜜雪冰城的雪王和霸王茶姬有了自己的孩子”……最近，一群“成精”的水果席卷短视频平台，它们被赋予人类的身材、五官和服饰，化身“渣男”、“绿茶”等身份，用极端化的人设演绎出轨、复仇等狗血剧情。

810.section: ## 抖快红B上最火的AI博主，在赚钱了吗？
810.para: 水果AI短剧刚在全网获得亿级播放的同时，其低俗化、猎奇化以及涉嫌侵权等问题，也随之浮出水面。

811.section: ## 抖快红B上最火的AI博主，在赚钱了吗？
811.para: 巴西、韩国等国家已加强管控，提高视频平台年龄分级，国内网信办则在4月底启动整治AI低俗内容专项行动，重点打击暴力、侵权乱象。

812.section: ## 抖快红B上最火的AI博主，在赚钱了吗？

813.section: ## 抖快红B上最火的AI博主，在赚钱了吗？
813.para: **AI既是生产力，也是要被一再重视底线的潘多拉魔盒。**

814.section: ## 抖快红B上最火的AI博主，在赚钱了吗？
814.para: 它把创作门槛从专业团队拉低到“一个人+一段提示词”，却也催生了擦边、低俗、批量制造的“电子垃圾”。

815.section: ## 抖快红B上最火的AI博主，在赚钱了吗？
815.para: 从“野蛮生长”到“合规求生”，AI内容创作者正站在一个分水岭上。

816.section: ## 抖快红B上最火的AI博主，在赚钱了吗？
816.para: 在这样的大背景下，那些在抖音、快手、小红书、B站上跑出来的AI博主们，到底赚钱了吗？他们是靠品牌广告、平台扶持、卖课收徒，还是转型做产品？

817.section: ## 抖快红B上最火的AI博主，在赚钱了吗？
817.para: **壹娱观察（ID：yiyuguancha）** 整理了四大平台上活跃度较高的十余位AI博主，从粉丝量、内容类型、商业模式三个维度试图剖析。

819.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
819.para: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态

820.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
820.para: 纵观当前各平台上的AI创作者，大致可以分为四类：AI工具测评与科普、AIGC创作、虚拟人/数字人博主、硬核技术与开发。

821.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
821.para: **第一类，AI工具测评与科普——流量快，变现稳。**

822.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
822.para: 这是最常见也最能“起量”的类型。

823.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
823.para: 博主实时测评最新AI产品，分享使用技巧和底层逻辑，帮助普通人快速上手。

824.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
824.para: “秋芝2046”是其中的典型代表，目前全网拥有245万粉丝，主要集中在抖音和B站。

825.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
825.para: 她曾是互联网产品经理，如今专注AI技术科普、工具评测与产品化落地。

826.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
826.para: 在抖音上，她点赞量最高的一期视频是盘点“2025年度好用AI工具”——将多款同类型产品横向对比，帮用户快速判断哪款真正值得投入。有网友评价：“她不跟你扯那些枯燥的理论，主打就是告诉你什么AI工具好用、怎么用好AI工具。”而在B站，她的身份更进一步：担任2026年B站首届AI春晚的总导演和主持人，与其他30多位UP主共创了一场AI含量百分百的春晚，视频播放量达1153万，成功入选“B站每周必看”。

827.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态

828.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
828.para: 可以说，AI工具测评与科普类博主天然踩中了两个商业逻辑。

829.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
829.para: 一是“流量快”——用户对“什么AI工具好用”有着持续且旺盛的信息焦虑，每一次新工具发布都是一次热点流量追踪；

830.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
830.para: 二是“变现稳”，当建立起“选品权威”的人设，后续无论是接AI产品的品牌广告、参与平台激励计划，还是通过付费社群或知识付费提供进阶教程，都有相对成熟且可持续的变现路径。

831.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
831.para: 以“秋芝2046”为例，抖音的横向测评爆款帮她聚拢了大众流量，B站的AI春晚深度共创则强化了她在行业内的专业声量。只要AI工具还在迭代，他们的内容就永远有需求。

832.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态

833.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
833.para: **第二类，AIGC创作——创意是灵魂，AI是工具。**

834.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
834.para: 无论AI产出的作品多么令人惊艳，本质上仍是工具，如果想借其进行内容创作，来自人类的创意仍是灵魂。

835.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
835.para: 当一只小猫穿着人类的衣服，经历挤地铁、加班与摸鱼，完美复刻职场状态时，这届年轻人终于迎来了专属自己的AI杀猪盘——而这，正是“荒蛋记录员”的独特魅力所在。

836.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
836.para: 博主借助AI工具，以vlog形式记录猫咪的日常，让猫咪成为当代年轻人的“电子嘴替”。

837.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
837.para: 观众看的不仅是萌宠，更是把自身情绪与向往投射其中，从而产生强烈的情感共鸣。截至目前，“荒蛋记录员”全网拥有78万粉丝，主要集中在抖音和B站。

838.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态

839.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
839.para: 热度最高的一期视频是小猫和小伙伴出来玩的vlog：几只AI生成的小猫一起拍低脂小视频，玩密室逃脱，逛游乐园。视频结尾一句“人，你也要快乐起来哦”，精准击中了观众的心弦。

840.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
840.para: 值得一提的是，在发布纯猫咪AI vlog之前，博主曾尝试在AI视频中加入人类角色，但效果远不如纯猫咪版本。或许观众只想没心没肺、把自己纯纯当做小猫活一回。

841.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
841.para: “WAI-你听”、“旧梦留声机”、“银河旅人”走的是不一样的路线，用AI生成人类为主角的剧情短片。

842.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
842.para: 其中出自“WAI-你听”的AI短片《纸手机》在清明期间刷屏各大内容平台，一个连“去世”都不懂的孩子，攥着攒下的15块钱，想买一部“纸手机”烧给带大他的奶奶。这条5分钟的视频上线两天播放量就突破千万，目前抖音点赞量176万、B站播放量423万、小红书点赞超10万。最令人惊讶的是，这部情感细腻到让无数网友落泪的短片，全片仅有手绘纸板手机是实拍道具，其余场景、人物、镜头均由AI生成，团队仅用3天就完成了从分镜到成片全部工作。

843.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态

844.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
844.para: “旧梦留声机”的《宝贝回家》在抖音获得823万点赞，“银河旅人”创作的聚焦留守儿童的《饭还热着》抖音获赞397万，都说明现在的AI生成内容不仅能制造“爽感”与“萌点”，同样可以承载深刻的社会关怀与情感温度。

845.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
845.para: 对于创作者而言，这更意味着更广阔的商业想象空间——打动大众情感的内容，天然具备破圈传播和品牌合作的潜力。

846.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
846.para: **第三类，AI虚拟博主——当AI有了自己的人设。**

847.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
847.para: 万物皆可养成系，AI主播也可以。

848.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
848.para: “鹅娘（ai团播版）”就是其中之一，57.9万粉丝全部集中在抖音。

849.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
849.para: 她的视频记录自己作为团播小白的一天：早起喝咖啡强制开机，骑着共享单车一路狂奔去公司，化妆装点门面……整个过程与真人团播主播几乎毫无差别，甚至还融入了水果AI短剧、猫咪vlog等最新热梗。

850.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
850.para: 有网友感叹：“这个视频简直跟AI生成的一样。”下方另一网友回复：“这不就是AI。”

851.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态

852.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
852.para: 此外，也有一些创作者尝试打造纯AI生成的虚拟偶像。

853.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
853.para: 比如AI TALK创始人汗青打造的AI虚拟偶像Yuri尤栗。Yuri并不是传统意义上人工建模的虚拟偶像，而是一位“AI原生”歌手。从外表设计、歌曲创作到短视频内容，几乎全部由AI生成。她挑染着蓝色长发，手持骷髅造型，仅出道MV就在B站获得135万播放。

854.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态

855.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
855.para: 出道不到一个月，户外品牌The North Face就主动找上门。2026年1月31日，Yuri获得北京经济技术开发区颁发的全国首个虚拟偶像身份认证，正式以“数字居民”身份落户北京经开区。这不仅意味着虚拟偶像的身份得到了官方认可，也预示AI生成的虚拟IP正在从流量红利转向商业确定性。

856.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
856.para: 只要人设有足够的粘性、情感连接足够强，AI虚拟博主的商业想象空间，或许比真人博主还要大。

857.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态

858.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
858.para: 北京经开区为Yuri颁发全国首个虚拟偶像身份认证

859.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
859.para: **第四类，AI技术与开发——硬核与深度。**

860.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
860.para: 这类博主由专业人士主导，分享AI领域的学术研究、代码实现和前沿技术动态，适合希望深入学习的进阶用户。

861.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
861.para: “跟李沐学AI”在这方面最具代表性。

862.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
862.para: 作为亚马逊自身首席科学家、BosonAI联合创始人，李沐从2021年就开始在B站分享AI技术的论文讲解，带网友丝进行AI深度学习的训练实操。目前，他的全网粉丝量超113万，其中112万都分布于B站。

863.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
863.para: 需要注意的是，李沐的模式可复制性极低，他并非纯粹的内容创作者，而是技术布道者。

864.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
864.para: 在商业化层面，他通过BosonAI公司为大客户做定制化模型，其内容更像是对个人品牌的增值，而非直接变现工具。

865.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态

866.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
866.para: 这类硬核的AI深度内容，往往需要系统性、长时间的学习，无法靠几分钟的短平快视频讲清楚。

867.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
867.para: 以李沐为例，他的视频最长超过一个半小时。

868.section: ## 四种AI博主，四种生存姿态
868.para: 因此，这类内容对传播平台有着特定的要求，更适合那些能够承载长视频、支持深度学习氛围的平台。

869.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
869.para: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解

870.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
870.para: 粉丝量是面子，钱袋子才是里子。从变现路径来看，主要分为以下四种：

871.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
871.para: **其一，品牌广告商单——头部玩家的常规打法。**

872.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
872.para: 这是AI博主最直接、最主流的变现方式。

873.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
873.para: 当AI工具成为互联网公司的核心竞争赛道时，AI测评博主就成了天然的广告投放对象。常见如“秋芝2046”在视频里提到的各种AI工具，以实测的形式提高产品声量。

874.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
874.para: 另一类变现方式，则是由AI内容衍生出的品牌合作。比如“WAI-你听”在今年母亲节前夕，发布了与olay合作的母亲节礼盒广告，视频内容由AI生成，却也展示出女儿与母亲深夜枕边话的亲密时刻。

875.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解

876.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
876.para: **其二，收徒与卖课——中腰部创作者的“现金流工厂”。**

877.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
877.para: 卖课是AI内容创作者的隐秘金矿。

878.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
878.para: 从“LT小狗日记【收徒】”这个账号名就能看出端倪，收徒本质上就是贩卖AI创作教程，“教你怎么用AI做内容赚钱”本身就成为了一门生意。

879.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
879.para: 该账号创作的AI短剧《比熊殿下她权倾天下》，讲述了一只比熊从福利院重返比熊国当公主掌权的故事。这类AI短剧的创作门槛并不高——不需要专业的动画团队，也不需要昂贵的拍摄设备，一个人借助几个AI工具，花上几小时就能生成一集。

880.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解

881.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
881.para: AI短剧《比熊殿下她权倾天下》

882.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
882.para: 正因门槛低、上手快，才催生了“收徒”模式的繁荣。一套定价几百元的“AI短剧变现课”，卖出几百份就是数万元的纯收入。这门生意的本质，是借“AI造富神话”收割普通人的知识焦虑。

883.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
883.para: **其三，自研AI产品——从博主到创始人的跃迁。**

884.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
884.para: 这属于更高阶的变现方式。

885.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
885.para: AI产品经理出身的“张咋啦”在今年1月发布了个人AI产品LongCut，完成了内容创作者到产品创始人的转型。

886.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
886.para: 跨界挑战在于，从“教人用AI”到“做出AI产品”之间有一条巨大的认知鸿沟。但它的潜力和影响力也远超单纯的内容变现，一旦产品跑通，商业价值呈指数级放大。

887.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解

888.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解

889.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
889.para: **其四，获得平台扶持——流量现金红利。**

890.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
890.para: 当AI博主摸索变现路径的同时，各大平台、产品也在用真金白银“抢人”。不仅有抖快B红，更包括即梦、可灵、小云雀等AI生成工具，都相继发布了创作激励计划，给予现金流量扶持，让创作者感受到赛道起飞前的早期红利。

891.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
891.para: 纵观这十余位活跃的AI博主，我们发现AI内容创作者的流量与收入，高度依赖于平台生态与内容类型的匹配度。

892.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
892.para: 抖音是流量的放大器，算法推荐机制让创意脑洞和工具测评类内容极易出圈；B站是硬核内容的主场，适合沉淀深度信任；小红书能够吸引到高单价客户，但涨粉慢，需要长期深耕内容质量，无法一夜爆红；快手则是短剧赛道的政策风口，可灵AI的创作者计划提供了真金白银的补贴。

893.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
893.para: 2026年的AI内容赛道，已经从“技术红利期”进入“内容深耕期”。

894.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
894.para: 流量依然在，钱也依然在，但只有那些真正理解平台规则、尊重内容底线、并能为用户提供独特价值的创作者，才能拿到那张长期饭票。

895.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
895.para: 本文来自微信公众号 [“壹娱观察”（ID：yiyuguancha）](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s?__biz=MzI0MjM2NTY4Mw==&mid=2247592364&idx=1&sn=7fbadc7bf0e8eba3c0c6478a9df7953e&chksm=e8c21cfc8b1052cc87b5b7f962b69d65fff531ee99b60790915913e27bd9eb472802d9f2b59a&scene=0&xtrack=1#rd)，作者：壹叔团队，36氪经授权发布。

896.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解

897.section: ## 赚钱了吗？四种变现路径拆解
897.para: 你都对不起你收集材料的时间

899.para: 更新：2026-11-14｜总纲。分篇文档是零件，这篇是装配图。

900.para: **前一层不成立，后一层做了也白做。**

901.para: 依据不是偏好，是因果先后： - **流量在先**：没有曝光，记忆无从产生（曝光效应 Zajonc 1968 的前提是"接触"）。 - **记忆在信任之前**：准社会关系（Horton & Wohl 1956）建立在"重复见到同一个人"之上，记不住就无从信任。 - **信任在成交之前**：B 端是高卷入决策，走中心路径（ELM 1986），没有论据与信任，报价只会被比价。 - **成交在转介绍之前**：没交付过，就没有可转述的事实。

902.para: 反过来做（先做转化、再补内容）的典型症状：简介挂满入口，但没有一条视频让人记住你是谁。

904.para: **要解决的问题**：让系统把你推给对的人，且他们没在前 3 秒划走。

905.para: **挂哪些理论** - 召回-排序-重排（[流量理论](流量理论-推荐到搜索.md)，Covington et al., RecSys 2016）——题材不清则召回阶段就没你。 - 探索-利用（同上，Sutton & Barto 1998）——新号会得到少量试探流量，但只够评估，不够起量。 - 好奇心缺口（[心理-02](心理-02-好奇心缺口.md)，Loewenstein 1994）——开头要开一个具体缺口。 - 高唤醒情绪（[传播理论](传播理论-情绪到说服路径.md)，Berger & Milkman 2012）——意外/敬畏促进传播，愤怒只带来情绪流量。 - 推荐流量 vs 搜索流量（[流量理论](流量理论-推荐到搜索.md)）——两套标题。 - 冷启动与养号（[02-新号冷启动](02-新号冷启动与养号.md)）——"养号"是【传闻】，不做。 - 口播与剪辑数值（[制作-01](制作-01-口播与剪辑手艺.md)）——280–320 字/分钟、每 3–5 秒一次画面变化。

906.para: **必须做的动作** 1. 前 5 条同一题材，标题与口播固定出现"智能体 / 客户现场 / 交付"。 2. 每条前 3 秒给一个具体反常，不出现人脸打招呼、不出现片头。 3. 每条只开一个好奇心缺口，15 秒内合上一半。 4. 每条 3–5 秒一次画面变化，字幕底边留 15%。

907.para: **怎么判断成了** - 5 秒完播率 ≥50%、完播率与同长度同类可比（后台可测）；外部通道**不可测**。 - 代理指标（可观测）：评论区出现"这啥情况/没看懂"之外的**具体追问**。

908.para: **最常见的死法**：开头自我介绍；标题写品类词（"AI 智能体分享"）；一条里开三个缺口；日更但题材乱跳。

909.para: **这层不成立时**：后面五层全部归零——没人看见，记忆、信任、成交都没有输入。

911.para: **要解决的问题**：看完之后，观众能用一个词/一句话说出你是谁。

912.para: **挂哪些理论** - 定位（[广告理论](广告理论-定位到说服.md)，Ries & Trout 1981）——占一个空位，不抢"AI 博主"。 - CBBE 联想网络（同上，Keller 1993）——单一维度反复强化才形成强联想。 - 口号结构（同上，Reeves 1961 USP + 口号要素）——短、可复读、指向一个利益。 - 重复曝光（同上，Zajonc 1968 / Bornstein 1989）——形式重复，内容不重复；倒 U。 - 可得性启发（同上，Tversky & Kahneman 1973）——反复同一场景，让"想起你"先于"比较你"。 - 模因（[传播理论](传播理论-情绪到说服路径.md)，Dawkins 1976 / Shifman 2014）——固定可被套用的句式。

913.para: **必须做的动作** 1. 主口号定一个（建议"AI 不听话的时候，我在场"），30 天不改。 2. 联动词只强化 A 组：现场 / 交付 / 跑通。 3. 每条结尾同一句式：「我让它做 X，它……」，让别人能套用。 4. 固定片头 0.5 秒同一动作。

914.para: **怎么判断成了** - 评论区有人用你的句式接话，或直接叫出你的定位词（可观测）。 - 主页访问率（后台可测）持续上升；品牌词搜索量**当前通道不可测**。

915.para: **最常见的死法**：每期换题材；今天讲技术、明天讲创业、后天讲生活；口号一周一改。

916.para: **这层不成立时**：观众记住了内容但记不住人——播放再高也换不来私信，第三层的信任没有对象可依附。

918.para: **要解决的问题**：让观众相信"这个人说的话有依据，且他真做过"。

919.para: **挂哪些理论** - 准社会关系（[心理-01](心理-01-准社会关系.md)，Horton & Wohl 1956）——持续出现 + 对镜头说话 + 私人细节。 - 叙事传输（[心理-03](心理-03-叙事传输.md)，Green & Brock 2000）——故事在前、道理在后，降低反驳。 - 中心路径（[传播理论](传播理论-情绪到说服路径.md)，ELM 1986）——给论据，不只给气氛。 - 直接说服（[广告理论](广告理论-定位到说服.md)）——每条一个可核对数字。 - 社会认同（同上，Cialdini 1984）——真实评价截图，不造假。 - 声望型地位（[人性-04](人性-04-地位理论.md)，Henrich & Gil-White 2001）——展示"我能干"，不宣告"我厉害"。 - 人性的弱点（[人性-01](人性-01-人性的弱点.md)，Carnegie 1936，【经验帖】）——让对方保住面子。

920.para: **必须做的动作** 1. 每条至少一个数字（跑了多少单、原来几小时、现在几分钟）。 2. 每条一个判断句，且是可反驳的（不是"AI 很重要"）。 3. 主动讲一次失败/判断错误，不每条都成功。 4. 不承诺效果（"省 80%""包学会"），只陈述事实。

921.para: **怎么判断成了** - 评论区出现 L2（求方法）或 L1（求定制/问价）原话（可观测，本项目的判定口径）。 - 私信中出现"我看了你那条 XX"（可观测）。

922.para: **最常见的死法**：只讲信息不给判断（变成教程搬运）；全是成功案例（不可信）；出现一次效果承诺（合规风险 + 信任反噬）。

923.para: **这层不成立时**：第四层"被找到"即使发生，找到的也只是一个报价页——没有信任的询价会直接进入比价，第五层成交率极低。

925.para: **要解决的问题**：当有人真的想解决这个问题时，能在哪找到你、且找到的是"人"不是"号"。

926.para: **挂哪些理论** - 搜索流量打法（[流量理论](流量理论-推荐到搜索.md)）——问题词标题。 - 免费流量三来源（同上）——推荐/搜索/社交各占一点。 - 注意力商品化（[人性-02](人性-02-注意力商品化.md)，Smythe 1977）——客户名单必须自己攥。 - 两级传播（[传播理论](传播理论-情绪到说服路径.md)，Lazarsfeld 1944）——B 端靠同行转述。 - 私域与公域承接（[增长理论](增长理论-AARRR到复购.md)）——公域获客、私域承接。

927.para: **必须做的动作** 1. 简介三行：身份一句话 / 做过什么 / 入口一句话，30 天不动。 2. 置顶放一条交付案例（不是自我介绍）。 3. 同一内容两套标题：推荐版写反常，搜索版写问题词，晚 3–7 天发。 4. 每条成片发 3–5 个同行/前同事，请他们转群。

928.para: **怎么判断成了** - 私信第一句出现"我搜 XX 找到你的"（可观测）。 - 主页访问 → 私信的转化率（可手工计：私信数 ÷ 主页访问，后台有访问数）。

929.para: **最常见的死法**：简介写满形容词但没有事实；置顶是自我介绍；所有标题只写反常，没有一条能被搜索命中。

930.para: **这层不成立时**：需求发生时找不到入口，第三层积累的信任无法兑现——流量停在"看过"，不会变成"联系过"。

932.para: **要解决的问题**：把"有兴趣"变成"有报价、有订单"。

933.para: **挂哪些理论** - 行为经济学（[心理-04](心理-04-行为经济学.md)，Kahneman & Tversky 1979 / 1974 / 2011）——锚定、框架、损失厌恶（系数被高估，不作精确常数）。 - FCB 网格（[广告理论](广告理论-定位到说服.md)，Vaughn 1980）——B 端属高卷入理性，信息:情绪 ≈ 7:3。 - 社会交换（[人性-05](人性-05-社会交换理论.md)，Homans 1958 / Blau 1964）——降低互动成本、提高回报确定性。 - 互惠利他（[人性-03](人性-03-互惠利他.md)，Trivers 1971）——先给三次再提要求。 - 转化路径限制（[待写] 转化路径）——私信/简介/评论区的合规边界。

934.para: **必须做的动作** 1. 报价先给锚点（完整版在前，轻量版在后），只给两个方案 + 一个参照。 2. 私信第一轮只要一句话场景，不要预算和电话。 3. 前 3 条内容不提任何转化；第 4 条起才出现"想要的私信我"。 4. 每条只提一个动作，不叠加赞/评/关注/私信。

935.para: **怎么判断成了** - 有效私信数（出现"多少钱/能不能做/什么价"）≥3 条；报价数、成单数、客单价可手工记。

936.para: **最常见的死法**：一上来甩报价；同时要四个动作；承诺效果；客户名单留在平台里。

937.para: **这层不成立时**：第六层没有交付事实可引用——转介绍无从发生，整个链路退化成"流量生意"。

939.para: **要解决的问题**：让交付过的客户愿意公开说一句，并带来下一个客户。

940.para: **挂哪些理论** - 互惠利他（[人性-03](人性-03-互惠利他.md)）——先给后取，长期关系成立。 - 社会认同（[广告理论](广告理论-定位到说服.md)，Cialdini 1984）——真实评价是最强证据。 - 声望型地位（[人性-04](人性-04-地位理论.md)）——被推荐的是"这个人靠谱"，不是"这个服务便宜"。 - 两级传播（[传播理论](传播理论-情绪到说服路径.md)）——B 端信息经同行中转。 - 复购与转介绍经济学（[增长理论](增长理论-AARRR到复购.md)，Reichheld 2003）——K 因子在客户数 <50 时**不适用**。

941.para: **必须做的动作** 1. 交付结束当天要一句可公开的评价（不要求好评，只要具体）。 2. 评价截图进置顶。 3. 每季度给老客户发一次"我看到一个跟你类似的问题"，不问单。 4. 不设计"推荐有礼"，量太小。

942.para: **怎么判断成了** - 老客户主动推荐数 ≥1；公开评价 ≥3 条。

943.para: **最常见的死法**：交付完即失联；只敢要好话；把转介绍做成返佣。

944.para: **这层不成立时**：每一单都要重新买流量，账号永远停在"获客"阶段，没有复利。

946.para: | 从 | 到 | 传导条件 | 断了会怎样 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 被看见 | 2 被记住 | 5 秒完播成立 + 固定识别元素 | 完播低 → 没人看到结尾 → 记忆无从建立 | | 2 被记住 | 3 被信任 | 记住之后还愿意看第二条 | 记不住 → 第二条被当陌生人 → 信任从零开始 | | 3 被信任 | 4 被找到 | 有信任 + 有入口 | 没入口 → 信任停在"关注"，不会变"联系" | | 4 被找到 | 5 被成交 | 找到的是人 + 有案例 | 主页空 → 从"找到"掉回零 | | 5 被成交 | 6 被转介绍 | 交付完成 + 主动索要评价 | 没交付 → 无事实可转述 |

947.para: **一句话**：这条链是串联电路，不是并联。断一层，后面全黑。

976.para: 4. **冷启动先给小流量，再按互动信号决定是否加推**。【经验帖】几乎所有运营课程都这么讲，但没人给出可复现的实验。 5. **起决定作用的信号是"完播 + 互动 + 关注"三项，权重顺序不明**。【经验帖】 6. **"账号权重"这个概念**：广泛流传，但**找不到官方原文**。【传闻】官方口径更接近"每条作品独立评估"，账号标签影响分发人群而非直接加权。 7. **垂直度影响初始人群准确度**：同一账号连续发同一题材，系统更快找到对的人。【经验帖】本项目侧证：合集型账号（AI编程自习室 272 条同题材）能稳定进入同类人群【实测】。

980.section: ## 四、对 FDE 账号意味着什么
980.para: 1. **前 5 条不要换题材**。系统靠题材找人群，换题材等于重新冷启动一次。动作：把 15 条排期里同一智能体的 4 条纵深放在前 10 条内。 2. **别指望"起号靠一条爆款"**。既然每条独立评估，就把资源放在"每条都能被同类人看完"，而不是押注单条。 3. **不要为"权重"做仪式性动作**（养号、点赞、完播别人的视频）。找不到依据的事不做。 4. **用"评论里有没有具体问题"判断加推质量**，比盯播放量可靠——播放量本来也看不到。

982.section: # 新号冷启动：前几条的推流特征与"养号"

983.para: 1. **官方没有"养号"这个概念，也没有任何"新号需要先养"的规则**。【官方】截至 2026-11，抖音创作者服务中心与社区规范中均无此表述。**"养号"整体属于【传闻】**。 2. **新号发布的作品同样进入推荐候选，不存在"新号先限流 7 天"的公开规则**。【官方】无此规则；该说法无出处。【传闻】 3. **账号的初始人群依赖内容标签**：同一账号连续发同类内容，系统更快找到对应人群。【经验帖】 4. **前几条播放低是常态，不是处罚**。本项目观察：AI 方向小号（冬风 48 粉、董哥 67 粉、鳌拜 70 粉）作品数 5–26 条，长期在百级播放。【实测】

988.section: ## 四、对这个账号意味着什么
988.para: 1. **不做任何"养号"动作**。注册完直接发第一条，不做点赞、完播、刷同类视频这些仪式。 2. **前 5 条固定同一题材**（智能体反常 + 客户现场），让系统一次打准标签。第 6 条起才允许换场景（如客户现场型）。 3. **前 5 条不要删**。哪怕播放只有几百，它们承担的是"给账号打标签"的功能，删了等于重来。 4. **不要一天发多条**。两天一更，避免同质内容被判定重复（见《账号矩阵与赛马》）。 5. **简介定稿后再发**。第一版简介（承接 AI 落地 · 智能体/自动化）在 D0 前写好，之后 30 天不动。

991.section: ## 一、有官方条文的行为（不要碰）
991.para: ## 一、有官方条文的行为（不要碰）

992.section: ## 一、有官方条文的行为（不要碰）
992.para: 1. **搬运**：直接下载他人视频二次上传、去水印后发布、录屏他人内容作为主体。【官方】《抖音社区自律公约》明确禁止侵犯著作权、搬运他人作品。 2. **重复/低质**：同一内容多次发布、拼接无意义素材、纯文字轮播、画面长期静止。【官方】公约中有"低质内容"条款。 3. **诱导互动**：以"点赞/关注/评论后才能…"、抽奖要求关注、诱导分享为条件的行为。【官方】公约与创作者规范明确禁止。 4. **诱导站外导流**：在视频、简介、评论区明示微信号/二维码/手机号引导加好友。【官方】公约与商业推广规范均有限制。 5. **虚假宣传**：承诺收益、夸大效果（"包学会""保证月入过万"）。【官方】广告法与平台规范。 6. **敏感领域无资质发布**：医疗诊疗建议、金融荐股、法律代理承诺等需资质的类目。【官方】平台类目资质要求。

994.section: ## 二、只有经验、没有条文的部分
994.para: 7. **"限流"的具体触发阈值**（几个播放、几次举报）：**未获取**。平台不公布，只能观测到"某条突然只有两位数播放"。 8. **敏感词库**：**未获取**。平台不公开词表，市面上的"敏感词大全"均为【传闻】，且随时失效。 9. **判定为重复的相似度标准**：**未获取**。无官方百分比。 10. **"擦边"与"专业内容"的边界**：靠人工审核，标准不公开。【经验帖】

995.para: | 说法 | 分级 | 说明 | | --- | --- | --- | | 说"微信"两个字就会被限流 | 【传闻】 | 真正的问题是"导流行为"，不是词本身 | | 视频里出现二维码必封 | 【经验帖】 | 大概率被限流/下架，不是必然封号 | | 提到竞品会被降权 | 【传闻】 | 无依据 | | 用 AI 生成内容会被限流 | 【传闻】 | 平台要求标注 AI 生成内容【官方】，标注本身不是处罚 |

996.section: ## 四、对 FDE 账号的高危点（按风险排序）
996.para: ## 四、对 FDE 账号的高危点（按风险排序）

997.section: ## 四、对 FDE 账号的高危点（按风险排序）
997.para: 1. **视频里出现客户系统界面/客户名字**——涉及客户隐私与商业信息，比"搬运"更危险。动作：所有客户画面打码，名称用"一家做 XX 的公司"。 2. **口播承诺效果**——"这套能帮你省 80% 人力"属于效果承诺。动作：改成可核对的事实句"这套在一家客户跑了 47 单，原来手工 3 小时"。 3. **简介/评论区留联系方式**——见《转化路径》一篇，这是最容易踩的一条。 4. **录屏里出现他人素材/音乐**——BGM 用平台曲库，不用下载的 mp3。动作：剪辑时只用抖音内置音乐。 5. **讲"企业怎么用 AI 替代员工"**——容易被判"就业歧视/负面引导"。动作：话术改成"把重复劳动交给系统"，不说"替代谁"。

998.section: ## 五、这个账号意味着什么
998.para: ## 五、这个账号意味着什么

999.section: ## 五、这个账号意味着什么
999.para: 1. **文案过一遍四问**：有没有承诺效果？有没有出现客户信息？有没有引导站外？有没有资质外内容（医疗/金融/法律建议）？ 2. **不写"包""保证""百分百""稳赚"**，这四个词是文案里最容易被判虚假宣传的。 3. **客户素材一律打码 + 化名**，并在视频里说一句"已获客户许可"（这句本身降低举报概率）。 4. **不做"评论区扣 1 领资料"**——这是诱导互动的典型形态，改成"想要的私信我"。

1000.section: # 主页包装与转化路径细则
1000.para: # 主页包装与转化路径细则

1001.section: # 主页包装与转化路径细则
1001.para: 更新：2026-11-14｜L1+L3｜**重要：头像/置顶/封面三项在本项目 40 个账号抽样中未能读到**（未登录主页元素不渲染，见 [包装核查](../../2026-11-14/packaging-check/outputs/01-packaging-check.md)），因此本节所有包装标准均为**经验推断**，无样本验证。

1002.para: | 标准 | 反例 | | --- | --- | | 真人正脸，肩部以上，脸部占画面 50–60% | 全身照（手机上认不出脸） | | 深色纯背景，与肤色有对比 | 白墙自拍（糊成一团） | | 表情中性偏放松，不看镜头里的自己 | 大笑/搞怪（专业感消失） | | 缩到 40px 仍能辨认为人脸 | 用 logo、风景、宠物、二维码 |

1003.para: 【经验推断】依据：头像在评论区、推荐页只显示极小尺寸，可辨识度优先于美感。

1004.para: - 格式：**称呼 + 定位词**，≤10 字（例："XX 做 AI 落地"）。 - 反例：「AI 爱好者」「科技博主」「XX ｜ 分享」「全栈工程师」——泛词无法被转述，也无法被搜索。

1006.para: | 行 | 内容 | 例 | | --- | --- | --- | | 第 1 行 | 身份 + 一个可验证事实 | 帮 3 家中小企业把 AI 落到流程里 | | 第 2 行 | 服务范围（不超过 3 项） | 智能体 / 流程自动化 / 现场交付 | | 第 3 行 | 入口（不写联系方式） | 案例在置顶 · 合作备注来意 |

1007.para: **反例**：写满形容词（"热爱技术、持续学习"）；写"V:xxx"（站外导流，见下节）；三行都在讲自己不讲对方能得到什么。

1008.para: - **第一条**：交付案例（前后对比 + 数字），不是自我介绍。 - **第二条**：一条最能代表判断力的视频。 - **第三条**：可选，服务说明。 - 反例：置顶自我介绍（没人关心你是谁，只关心你解决过什么）。

1010.para: - 工作场景照（工位、客户现场），压暗 30%，不与头像抢视觉；不放带文字的营销图。 - 反例：纯文字 slogan 背景图（在手机上被裁切，只看到半个字）。

1011.para: **验收**：让一个陌生人看主页 3 秒，说出"这人做什么的"。说不出就重做第 1/3 行。

1013.para: | 入口 | 能做什么 | 限制 / 风控触发点 | | --- | --- | --- | | **私信** | 文字、图片、语音；可设自动回复 | 未关注时条数受限【经验帖】；发微信号/手机号/二维码易被拦截；批量群发易判营销 | | **评论区** | 置顶一条、回复 | 评论里写"加微信""V:xxx""私我发你"易被删或折叠【经验帖】；"扣1""评论区留言领资料"属诱导互动【官方】 | | **主页跳转** | 个人号仅站内；企业号可挂官网/联系电话/POI | 个人号无外链权限【官方】；简介写联系方式属导流【官方】限制 | | **企业号** | 认证后可挂电话、官网、地址、私信关键词回复 | 需营业执照；认证后内容仍受同一套社区规范约束 |

1014.para: **话术红旗（会被判站外导流）**：加微信 / V: / 威信 / 私我发你 / 扫码 / 转账 / 支付宝 / 手机号分段写。

1015.para: **可用的替代写法**： - 「案例在置顶」——把流量留在站内。 - 「评论区说下你的场景」——先产生对话，再私信。 - 「合作备注来意」——筛人，不写联系方式。

1016.para: **顺序原则**：公开区只做"引发对话"，联系方式只在私信里、且对方先开口后给。

1017.section: # 内容营销漏斗：从曝光到成交的损耗点
1017.para: # 内容营销漏斗：从曝光到成交的损耗点

1018.section: # 内容营销漏斗：从曝光到成交的损耗点
1018.para: 更新：2026-11-14｜L1 知识 + L3 战术｜每段转化率：**未获取**（无后台数据）

1019.para: | 段 | 转化动作 | 典型损耗点 | 该用什么内容 | 怎么测 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 曝光 | 被推荐到 | 题材不垂直 → 召回没你 | 固定题材 + 固定词 | 播放量（后台） | | 2 停留 | 3 秒不划走 | 开头自我介绍、无画面变化 | 反常第一帧 | 2 秒/5 秒跳出（后台） | | 3 认同 | 看完并记住 | 只讲信息、无判断 | 一次反常 + 一句判断 | 完播率、主页访问率（后台） | | 4 关注 | 关注/收藏 | 记不住人、无固定句式 | 固定口号、固定场景 | 涨粉数、收藏数 | | 5 私信 | 主动联系 | 没有入口、门槛太高 | 置顶案例 + 一句话引导 | **私信数（手工记）** | | 6 成交 | 付款 | 无报价锚、无案例、砍价失守 | 报价单 + 案例视频 | 报价数、成单数、客单价（手工记） |

1021.para: - **第 1 段损耗**：不是内容差，是**系统不知道把你推给谁**（题材乱）。 - **第 2 段损耗**：开头在"介绍自己"而不是"给事实"。 - **第 3 段损耗**：信息型内容被收藏，但不产生信任（收藏≠信任）。 - **第 4 段损耗**：观众记住内容，记不住人（没有固定符号）。 - **第 5 段损耗**：观众想联系但**找不到入口**，或觉得"问了会被推销"。 - **第 6 段损耗**：报价没有锚、没有案例、第一次砍价就让步。

1022.section: ## 三、各段内容的配比（一周 3 条）
1022.para: ## 三、各段内容的配比（一周 3 条）

1023.section: ## 三、各段内容的配比（一周 3 条）
1023.para: | 段 | 条数 | 形态 | | --- | --- | --- | | 1–2 曝光/停留 | 每条都要满足 | 前 3 秒反常 | | 3 认同 | 2 条 | 反常 + 判断 + 数字 | | 4 关注 | 每条都要满足 | 固定句式/口号 | | 5 私信 | 每 4 条 1 条 | 结果型（前后对比 + 入口） | | 6 成交 | 不进内容 | 私信里完成 |

1024.section: ## 四、测法（能测的测，测不到的别编）
1024.para: ## 四、测法（能测的测，测不到的别编）

1025.section: ## 四、测法（能测的测，测不到的别编）
1025.para: - **可测**：播放、完播、5 秒跳出、涨粉、主页访问（创作者后台）；私信数、报价数、成单数（手工表）。 - **不可测**：曝光到停留的真实转化（无曝光数）、关注后的留存曲线、私信到成交的行业基准。 - **替代测法**：算**每段相对上周的变化**，不跟"行业平均"比——行业数据全部**未获取**。

1026.section: ## 五、对这个账号意味着什么
1026.para: ## 五、对这个账号意味着什么

1027.section: ## 五、对这个账号意味着什么
1027.para: 1. **每周只盯一段**：第 1 周盯第 2 段（开头），第 2 周盯第 5 段（私信），不全都看。 2. **第 5 段的动作最便宜**：置顶加一条案例 + 评论置顶加需求模板，成本 10 分钟，收益最直接。 3. **第 6 段不在内容里做**，一律进私信，按接单 SOP 走。 4. **不追"行业转化率"**，只比自己上周——行业数字一个都没拿到。

1028.section: # 完播率怎么看才算正常
1028.para: # 完播率怎么看才算正常

1029.section: # 完播率怎么看才算正常
1029.para: 更新：2026-11-14｜L1｜**不给"及格线"数字**：任何"完播 30% 算合格"的说法都找不到官方或可信出处，标【传闻】，本库不采用。

1031.para: 1. **跟自己比**：同类型、同时长的历史中位数。低于自己的中位数 20% 以上 = 异常。 2. **跟同长度比**：35 秒的完播率天然高于 3 分钟，**跨时长比较没有意义**。只跟"自己同类同长度"比。

1032.section: ## 二、三个口径（先分清再看）
1032.para: ## 二、三个口径（先分清再看）

1033.section: ## 二、三个口径（先分清再看）
1033.para: | 指标 | 含义 | 用法 | | --- | --- | --- | | 5 秒完播率 | 开头是否成立 | **最该看的第一个数** | | 完整播放率 | 内容是否撑得住 | 与时长绑定看 | | 平均播放时长 | 观众在哪掉 | 配合进度条曲线找掉点 |

1035.para: 1. 5 秒完播低于自己同类中位数 → **开头问题**，换第一句，不换选题。 2. 5 秒正常但完整播放低 → **中段问题**，看曲线掉点，砍掉那一段。 3. 两个都正常但互动为 0 → **不是完播问题**，是内容没有可讨论的判断。

1037.para: - 平台官方"合格线"：**未获取**，不存在公开标准。 - 行业平均完播率：**未获取**，各家口径不一（是否算重播、是否算 3 秒）。 - 竞品完播率：**未获取**，外部不可见。

1038.para: 1. 建一张"自己历史表"：同类型同时长的 5 秒完播中位数，作为唯一基准。 2. 每条只跟这张表比，不跟网上数字比。 3. 低于中位数 20% 才判异常，**不因为"感觉低"就改**。

1039.section: # 七大平台对照：用户结构、内容形态、推荐逻辑、商业目标
1039.para: # 七大平台对照：用户结构、内容形态、推荐逻辑、商业目标

1040.section: # 七大平台对照：用户结构、内容形态、推荐逻辑、商业目标
1040.para: 更新：2026-11-14｜L1 知识｜分级：除注明外均为【经验帖】，**具体比例与成本数据一律未获取**

1041.section: # 七大平台对照：用户结构、内容形态、推荐逻辑、商业目标
1041.para: > 说明：本轮没有做平台侧实测，也没有拿到官方人群报告。以下"用户结构"为行业通行描述，**不是数据**；凡是数字的地方都写未获取。

1043.para: | 平台 | 用户结构（描述性，非数据） | 内容形态偏好 | 推荐与分发逻辑 | 适合的商业目标 | 起量难度 | 投放成本 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **抖音** | 全年龄、下沉+城市均有；泛娱乐底盘大 | 3 秒抓人、强节奏、真人出镜 | 强推荐、兴趣分发，单条独立评估 | 快速获客、接单引流 | 中（内容要求高，起量快） | 未获取 | | **视频号** | 偏中年以上、微信生态内；社交关系链强 | 口播、知识、情感、慢节奏 | **社交推荐权重高**（朋友点赞会外溢），叠加算法 | B 端信任、私域承接 | 中偏高（无社交启动则慢） | 未获取 | | **小红书** | 女性占比高（具体比例未获取）；一二线、消费决策前搜索 | 图文/短视频，重"有用+好看"，标题即搜索词 | 搜索 + 推荐双引擎，**搜索占比显著** | 种草、服务获客（本地/专业服务） | 中（图文比视频容易起） | 未获取 | | **B站** | 年轻、学生与初级职场为主；长内容耐受度高 | 3–20 分钟，教程/评测/深度 | 推荐 + 搜索 + 关注，**完播与互动权重大** | 建立专业信誉、长尾搜索 | 高（制作成本高） | 未获取 | | **知乎** | 职场、专业人群；决策前检索 | 图文长答、专栏 | 搜索

1045.para: 1. **只有抖音是"纯推荐"起量**；视频号靠社交、小红书靠搜索、知乎靠问题页、B站靠完播。**同一套内容逻辑不能平移。** 2. **B 端客户在视频号/微信生态，不在抖音**。这是本账号最需要正视的一条：抖音能给流量，但决策人可能在微信里。 3. **搜索型平台（小红书/知乎/B站）适合"被找到"，推荐型平台（抖音/快手）适合"被看见"**——对应主干第 1 层与第 4 层。

1046.section: ## 三、对 FDE 账号意味着什么
1046.para: ## 三、对 FDE 账号意味着什么

1047.section: ## 三、对 FDE 账号意味着什么
1047.para: 1. **主战场仍是抖音**（第 1 层要量），**视频号作为第二落点**（第 4 层要人）。 2. **小红书可以只做图文**：把一条视频的判断句 + 3 张截图做成笔记，成本 20 分钟，占搜索位。 3. **B 站/知乎暂不做**：制作与写作成本高，当前产能撑不住（见产能约束）。 4. **微博/快手不做**：与"专业翻译"人设不匹配。 5. 所有"投放成本差异"本轮**未获取**，要用必须先实测 100 元级小额投放。

1048.section: # 心理补充：自我呈现、从众、门槛、旁观、观众心理
1048.para: # 心理补充：自我呈现、从众、门槛、旁观、观众心理

1049.section: # 心理补充：自我呈现、从众、门槛、旁观、观众心理
1049.para: 更新：2026-11-14｜L1 知识｜实验类标年份，重复验证危机处标注

1051.para: - **出处**：Erving Goffman,《The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life》，1959。 - **核心主张**：**前台**是表演区（有观众、有剧本、有道具），**后台**是准备区。印象管理 = 控制前台的信息流；**崩塌发生在后台泄漏**。 - **适用**：人设号的全流程。 - **失效**：把一切都当表演会失去真实感；观众对"明显在演"极度敏感。 - **崩塌五大诱因**：① 后台画面意外入镜（聊天记录、他人）；② 被追问专业细节接不住；③ 前后说法矛盾；④ 商业化的速度超过信任积累；⑤ 线下接触与线上人设不符。 - **动作**：每条只演"判断与现场"，不演"能力"；录制前清空桌面与通知；建立"不能说的话"清单（没做过的项目、没验证的数字）。

1053.para: - **出处**：Solomon Asch 线段实验，1951；Cialdini,《Influence》，1984。 - **核心主张**：在不确定时，人用他人行为判断正确行为；**公开的多数意见会压制个人判断**（Asch 中约 1/3 被试跟随明显错误的答案）。*重复验证：Asch 效应在后续跨文化重复中存在，但效应量随情境差异很大。* - **适用**：评论区氛围、置顶、案例展示。 - **失效**：受众是专业决策者时，从众让位于专业判断；造假被识破后反噬更强。 - **动作**：① 置顶一条"已有客户的问题"建立多数感；② 评论区先自己回一条有信息量的，定调；③ 不刷量、不买评（识破即毁）。

1055.para: - **出处**：Jonathan Freedman & Scott Fraser, "Compliance without Pressure: The Foot-in-the-Door Technique", *JPSP*, 1966。 - **核心主张**：先答应小请求的人，更容易答应后续大请求（自我形象一致性）。*重复验证：效应稳健但效应量中等，且需两次请求间隔不长。* - **适用**：从看到问的阶梯。 - **失效**：第一次请求太唐突或与后续无关时失效。 - **动作（三级阶梯）**：① 看（0 成本）→ ② 评论区二选一（一句话，如"A 还是 B"）→ ③ 私信"一句话说你的场景"。**不跳级**：视频里直接喊报价等于让对方第一次就付最高成本。

1057.para: - **出处**：John Darley & Bibb Latané, 1968（责任分散）。 - **核心主张**：在场人越多，个体越不行动——责任被分散。*后续元分析（Fischer et al. 2011）显示效应存在但弱于原研究，在危险情境中更强；网络情境的适用性有限。* - **适用**：解释"播放高但没人问"。 - **失效**：一对一场景（私信）不适用；有明确指令时效应消失。 - **动作**：① 明确点名而非泛问——"如果你也在做 XX，回我一句"；② 给单一出口（只留一个动作）；③ 主动私信前 20 个互动者，把"公共场合"变成"一对一"。

1059.para: - **注意力**：短视频的注意力以秒计，前 3 秒决定去留【经验帖】；"注意力时长 8 秒"的说法**无可靠出处，标【传闻】**。 - **情绪唤起**：高唤醒（意外、敬畏）促进记忆与分享（Berger & Milkman 2012，见传播篇）；低唤醒（平静）不利传播。 - **峰值-终值规则**：Kahneman 等 1993 年的体验记忆研究——人对一段经历的评价取决于**峰值**与**结尾**，不是平均。*注意：原研究基于疼痛/体验实验，外推到 30 秒视频属于类比，非验证。* - **动作**：① 一条视频只设一个峰值（反常那一刻）；② 结尾必须是判断句，不能是"就这样"；③ 不用平淡的收尾音乐。

1077.section: ### 怎么改才不算搬运（同一素材）
1077.para: **结论**：同一素材想多号发，**重拍比重剪安全**；纯切片+改标题仍是搬运【经验帖】。

1078.para: - 一个人维护：**1 个主号 + 1 个备份号**，不做 3 个以上（内容产能不够，必然同质）。 - 备份号用途：主号被限流时的临时出口，**不发同一条内容**，发同题材的不同案例。 - 多号风险：同设备登录多号易被关联【经验帖】；一机一号更稳。

1092.section: ## 一、人设怎么搭：真实与表演的边界
1092.para: **划法**：**能力不能演，态度可以演；经历不能编，表达可以设计。** **具体到本账号**：可以设计"每条都在现场"的呈现方式，但不能编造没做过的项目；一旦被同行追问架构细节，人设当场破。

1098.section: ## 三、内容资产化（单条 → 可复用资产）
1098.para: 1. **判断句**（一句可独立传播的结论）→ 进选题库、进简介、进小红书图文。 2. **案例卡**（客户场景 + 数字 + 前后对比）→ 进报价单、置顶、私信材料。 3. **开头模板**（验证有效的第一句）→ 进"开头库"，复用结构不复用内容。 4. **客户问题**（评论区/私信原话）→ 进选题库，下一条的选题来源。

1099.section: ## 三、内容资产化（单条 → 可复用资产）
1099.para: **判断标准**：一条视频如果只贡献了播放，没有产出以上四样中的任何一样，就是消耗品，不是资产。

1100.section: ## 四、危机公关处置流程（四步，按顺序）
1100.para: ## 四、危机公关处置流程（四步，按顺序）

1101.section: ## 四、危机公关处置流程（四步，按顺序）
1101.para: 1. **2 小时内**：不删、不辩论，先确认事实（是不是我们的问题）。 2. **当天**：发一条简短说明——**事实 + 我们做了什么 + 什么时候给结果**，不解释动机。 3. **48 小时**：给补救方案（退款/重做/补偿），私下完成，不公开拉扯。 4. **一周后**：把处理结果做成一条内容（如果客户同意），转成信任资产；不同意就沉默。

1102.section: ## 四、危机公关处置流程（四步，按顺序）
1102.para: **三条禁忌**：删评、对喷、找水军。任何一个都会把"专业问题"变成"人品问题"。

1103.section: ## 五、对这个账号意味着什么
1103.para: ## 五、对这个账号意味着什么

1104.section: ## 五、对这个账号意味着什么
1104.para: 1. **每条固定"现场"元素**（客户现场、工位、屏幕），这是可演的前台；项目细节必须真实。 2. **当前在 0 识别期**：只做固定句式 + 固定题材，不接广告、不卖课。 3. **每条必须产出四样资产中的至少一样**，否则这条白拍。 4. **危机流程打印出来贴在墙上**，出事时按顺序走，不临场反应。 5. **阶段判断看私信问价比例**，不看粉丝数——粉丝可以买，问价不能。

1106.para: 更新：2026-11-14｜L2 战略｜分级：【文献】为教材/论文，数据均未获取

1108.para: **细分变量（选 3 个就够，多了切不出可触达的人群）** 1. **身份**：同行 / 中小企业老板 / 个体经营者 2. **痛点强度**：已经在花钱解决 / 知道有问题但没预算 / 不觉得是问题 3. **决策链长度**：自己拍板 / 需要合伙人 / 需要走采购

1109.para: **判断细分是否成立的标准**：这群人**能不能在同一个地方被触达**（同一个平台、同一类社群）。触达不到的细分，等于没分。

1111.para: | 维度 | 同行（AI 从业者） | 中小企业老板 | 个体经营者 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 支付意愿 | 低（自己会做，只买课） | **高**（买结果，不买过程） | 中（预算小，但要现成） | | 决策链 | 自己 | 自己或 +1 合伙人 | 自己 | | 内容偏好 | 技术细节、源码、架构 | 成本、案例、同行怎么做 | 省时间、能不能马上用 | | 客单价（经验推断） | 几百（课） | 1–3 万 | 2,000–8,000 | | 触达难度 | 低（平台推荐即达） | 中（抖音少，视频号多） | 低（抖音/小红书） | | 最大风险 | 只叫好不付费 | 起量慢、信任门槛高 | 售后重、要求多 |

1112.para: **数据缺口**：三类人群的真实支付分布、转化率、客单价分布——全部**未获取**，上表客单价是经验推断。

1113.section: ## 三、支付意愿怎么判断（三个可执行方法）
1113.para: ## 三、支付意愿怎么判断（三个可执行方法）

1114.section: ## 三、支付意愿怎么判断（三个可执行方法）
1114.para: 1. **看他已经在为什么付钱**：在招人（说明有人工成本）、在用外包（说明接受外部服务）、在买 SaaS（说明有预算科目）。 2. **问过去 12 个月**：「这类事你们去年花过多少钱？」——比问"你预算多少"有效。 3. **看谁签字**：签字人不是使用者时，支付意愿取决于"能不能向老板交代"，内容要给可汇报的材料。

1119.section: ## 五、定位陈述（一句话模板）
1119.para: > 为**已经有 AI 想法但落不了地的中小企业**，提供**从流程诊断到系统上线的一次交付**，使他们**在不增加人手的前提下把重复劳动交出去**；不同于**教程号和外包公司**，因为**我到场做过，且能给出可核对的前后数字**。

1120.section: ## 六、对这个账号意味着什么
1120.para: ## 六、对这个账号意味着什么

1121.section: ## 六、对这个账号意味着什么
1121.para: 1. **人群先选"中小企业老板"**（支付意愿最高），同行作为流量池而非客户。 2. **每条内容回答老板的三个问题**：这要花多少钱、跟我像不像、做完谁在用。 3. **竞争地图只占一个格**：深 + 到场。任何"不到场"的活（纯咨询、纯卖课）都不接。 4. **定位陈述写进简介第一行**，30 天不改。 5. 支付意愿的三问写进接单 SOP 的第 2 步（现在是"需求三问"，可加一问"去年花过多少钱"）。

1123.para: 不替你选。每个给：选项、前置条件、代价、判断依据。

1124.para: | 选项 | 前置条件 | 代价 | 适合什么情况 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **只做抖音** | 单平台内容能力足够；能接受一条腿走路 | 平台风险集中；一次限流=获客归零 | 起步期，先验证内容结构 | | **抖音 + 视频号** | 有微信生态；愿意为视频号重剪（竖屏节奏更慢） | 每周多 1–2 小时；两套数据要分别复盘 | 客户多在微信里、B 端为主 | | **多平台分发**（抖音+B站+小红书） | 有剪辑人力；能接受"一稿通发无效"的改写成本 | 每条内容要做 2–3 个版本；数据碎片化 | 有内容团队、或需要长期搜索流量 |

1125.para: **判断依据**：客户从哪来。B 端老板多在微信/视频号；技术同行在 B 站；女性消费与职场在小红书。**先看你的客户在哪个池子里，再看内容能力。**

1126.para: | 选项 | 前置条件 | 代价 | 内容后果 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **同行（AI 从业者）** | 内容要够硬；能接受"看的人不买" | 流量高、转化低；易滑成教程号 | 讲技术细节，粉丝涨得快，私信多为"求教程" | | **中小企业老板** | 能讲业务语言；有可展示的交付案例 | 起量慢；需要更强的信任建设 | 讲成本与结果，播放低但私信质量高 | | **个体经营者** | 客单要低、交付要标准化 | 客单价低、要量；售后重 | 讲"一个人怎么省时间"，适合标准包 |

1127.para: **判断依据**：你现有案例的客户是谁。案例决定人群，人群决定话术，反着做会做出"同行叫好、客户不来"的账号。

1128.para: | 选项 | 前置条件 | 代价 | 现金流特征 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **纯服务** | 有 3 个案例；能约束范围 | 产能即天花板；收入不稳 | 预付+尾款，波动大 | | **服务 + 标准包** | 同一需求被问过 3 次；能定死范围 | 客户会说"不够定制" | 单价降、成交率升、交付可复制 | | **服务 + 课程** | 有成体系方法；有答疑产能 | **稀释"我能替你落地"的定位**；退款风险 | 一次性收款，前期投入大 |

1129.para: **判断依据**：需求重复度。同一需求出现 3 次以上才做标准包；课程放到第 2 年，且只作为私域转化物，不公开卖。

1131.para: - 选"只做抖音 + 同行" → 流量快、转化慢，必须靠标准包承接。 - 选"抖音+视频号 + 中小企业老板" → 起量慢但私信质量高，适合纯服务。 - 选"多平台 + 个体经营者" → 必须标准包 + 低客单，否则产能撑不住。

1132.para: **不要同时选最重的一档**（多平台 + 老板 + 课程），一个人做不了三件事。

1134.para: 更新：2026-11-14｜L1 知识 + L2 战略｜数据缺口：真实毛利、获客成本均未获取

1136.para: | 维度 | 卖服务 | 卖产品（SaaS/工具） | 卖课程 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 边际成本 | **高**（每单都要人） | 低（复制近乎零） | 低（录一次卖多次） | | 规模上限 | 取决于人数 | 理论上无上限 | 取决于流量 | | 前期投入 | 低 | 高（研发 6–18 个月，经验推断） | 中（录制 1–2 个月） | | 现金流 | 预付+尾款，波动大 | 订阅，前期负现金流 | 一次性，前期投入大 | | 失败模式 | 产能撑爆 / 客户集中 | 退化成定制外包 | 与"我能落地"定位冲突 | | 对本账号适配 | **主线** | 第 2 年之后 | 只作私域转化物 |

1137.para: | 方法 | 怎么算 | 适用 | 风险 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **成本加成** | (工时 × 时薪) ÷ (1 − 毛利率) | 首次报价、无参照时 | 算不出工时就会亏；客户不认你的成本 | | **价值定价** | 按客户节省的成本/收益定价，取 10–30% | 有明确可量化收益（省人工、省时间） | 需要能算清客户的账；算错会被质疑 | | **竞争定价** | 参照同行报价，上下浮动 | 客户在比价、品类成熟 | 越比越低，滑进价格战 |

1138.para: **本账号的顺序**：先用成本加成算底线 → 用价值定价报出去 → 用竞争定价只做校验（不跟价）。

1140.para: 1. **预付 50% 才开工**，尾款验收 7 天内。 2. **单客户收入占比 ≤40%**（见品牌风险篇）。 3. **保留 3 个月固定支出的现金**，服务型收入的波动比想象大。

1142.para: - 固定：设备（一次性）、软件订阅、场地。 - 变动：交付工时（最大项）、外包剪辑（如有）。 - **毛利 = 报价 − 交付工时 × 时薪 − 外包**。经验推断毛利率 50–60%，**未验证**。

1143.section: ## 五、对这个账号意味着什么
1143.para: ## 五、对这个账号意味着什么

1144.section: ## 五、对这个账号意味着什么
1144.para: 1. **主线卖服务**，标准包解决"每单重新估工时"的问题；产品与课程都不在前 6 个月做。 2. **报价三步**：成本算底线（不低于 X）→ 价值定价报（按客户省的钱算）→ 不跟竞争对手的价。 3. **每单记工时**，3 单后回头校正时薪——现在的毛利率是推断，不是事实。 4. **现金规则写进合同**：预付 50%、验收 7 天、单客户 ≤40%。
